Homepage7487%https://join.frndlytv.com/
Full-scroll Frndly TV homepage leading with an affordability claim and free 7-day trial CTA, backed by plan pricing starting at $6.99/mo and an extensive channel grid.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Get the visitor to start a free 7-day trial of Frndly TV by presenting plans, channel lineup, device compatibility, testimonials, and pricing.
Primary CTA: Start Free Trial
Offer: Free 7-Day Trial
Message match: The page is a full-featured homepage that leads with the same affordability and free-trial message likely in the ad, providing a reasonably consistent destination, though it is a long-scroll homepage rather than a focused conversion page.
Trust: Real Stories from Real Families testimonial section, 50+ channel logos displayed, Compatible with Roku, Samsung, Fire TV, VIZIO, Chromecast, Android TV
Friction: Very long scroll page with many sections before reaching pricing, Multiple CTAs across the page may dilute focus
What works
  • Clear price anchoring with three-tier plan comparison ($6.99, $7.99, $9.99)
  • Free 7-day trial prominently and repeatedly offered
  • Channel grid shows breadth of content upfront
What it misses
  • No sticky or above-fold pricing — visitor must scroll far to see cost
  • No urgency or scarcity signals to compel immediate sign-up
  • Hero section CTA button is small relative to the large headline text

Homepage11%https://sling.com/
Sling TV homepage anchored to FIFA World Cup 2026 urgency, presenting five plan tiers from $19.99 and flexible short-term pass options to drive subscription sign-ups.
Landing-page analysis
Page intent: Convert visitors to sign up for a Sling TV subscription plan, anchored by FIFA World Cup 2026 sports content, by presenting plan tiers, channel availability, and flexible pass options.
Primary CTA: Get sling
Offer: 7-Day Pass, 2-Day Pass, and 1-Month Prepay flexible subscription options; free trial mentioned in a banner
Message match: The page has a strong seasonal/event-based focus on FIFA World Cup 2026 rather than a generic homepage feel — it is timely and specific, making it an effective destination for a sports-oriented ad, though it still functions as a full plan-selection homepage.
Trust: 'Watch TV, 100% free' Freestream promotion badge, Compatible devices shown (Roku, LG, VIZIO), Trending channel logos (ESPN, CNN, TNT, TBS, USA, FS1, FOX and others)
Friction: Multiple plan tiers with different price points ($19.99, $19.99, $34.99, $45.99, $45.99) may cause decision paralysis, Dense pricing table with many rows requires careful reading, Very long page with extensive channel and FAQ section in footer area
What works
  • Event-driven hero (FIFA World Cup 2026) creates immediate relevance and urgency
  • Flexible subscription framing (7-Day Pass, 2-Day Pass, 1-Month Prepay) lowers commitment barrier
  • Freestream 'Watch TV, 100% free' cross-promotion adds perceived value
What it misses
  • Five plan tiers shown simultaneously is overwhelming — no clear recommended plan highlighted
  • No customer reviews or social proof visible above the fold
  • Pricing for the hero offer ($19.99) is buried in a subhead rather than prominently featured

Philo Competitive Briefing — 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-15 — generated 2026-06-15T18:06:46+00:00 (briefing id 1)
## TL;DR

- **Philo's creative posture is split two ways**: roughly half the ad corpus sells the bundle/service ("tons of great TV, one subscription") and half promotes specific shows (Tyler Perry titles, BET, ALLBLK, HBO Max, HISTORY, MTV). Neither lane includes a price-comparison CTA or an explicit price anchor in most ads — a gap that Frndly and Sling are actively exploiting.
- **Frndly TV is Philo's most direct price-pressure threat**: every single Frndly ad opens with "$6.99/mo" and a 7-day free trial. Their top-ranked ad has run 323 days. At $25/mo, Philo has a value story to tell against $6.99 — it just isn't telling it.
- **Sling and Fubo have ceded the "entertainment" segment entirely to chase the FIFA World Cup** (Jun 11–Jul 19). Sling is also rolling out a new $19.99/mo "Essentials" tier anchored on ESPN. Neither is advertising into Philo's comfort-TV audience right now, creating a brief window.
- **Hulu is the only rival running a structured bundle narrative** — the Disney+/Hulu duo at $12.99/mo is in dozens of active ads. This is the premium framing Philo's Bundle+ ($33/mo with HBO Max/Starz) competes against, but Philo isn't naming the comparison.
- **YouTube TV has zero active Meta ads** in this snapshot. No competitive pressure from that vector at the moment.

---

## What Changed by Competitor

**Philo** — Baseline posture: two campaign tracks running in parallel. The "always-on" acquisition track uses interchangeable "Get tons of great TV / one subscription" copy (e.g., ads 1432021271313610, 800982826400755, running 87 days at high popularity). The content-promotion track spotlights specific shows — Tyler Perry's Sistas (top-ranked at 87 days), Divorced Sistas, Bridezillas, Love & Hip Hop Miami, Power Book III on Starz, Euphoria via HBO Max — to drive trial from genre- and personality-specific audiences. Creator/influencer partnerships (Eden Yonas, 365binge, Big Teezus) are live under the `asc-facebook-ihbc-essential` campaign. Winback retargeting is also active across both tracks (`winback-facebook-retargeting`). No price anchor appears in most ads; the lone exception is ad 1487361086172161 ("plans starting at $25/mo").

**Frndly TV** — Baseline posture: price-led, channel-name-dropped. Every ad leads with "$6.99/mo" or "50+ channels from $6.99/mo" and a 7-day free trial. Channel-specific creative covers Hallmark, Lifetime, A&E, HISTORY, Great American Family, and VICE. Premiere-event ads are live for Lifetime films ("Kidnapped in Her Own Home," "Single Black Tenant" 6/27, "Thou Shall Not Commit Adultery" 6/6, "Love, Again"). Their top-ranked ad (1697315644306958) has been running 292 days. Frndly overlaps directly with Philo on HISTORY, Lifetime, and A&E targeting.

**Sling TV** — Baseline posture: three legs. (1) FIFA World Cup 2026 (FOX/FS1, Jun 11–Jul 19), running the largest share of current creative, with influencer formats (Briankearneyy, Jack Greenberg, Golfshopthisischris). (2) A newly introduced "Sling Essentials" tier at $19.99/mo anchored on ESPN — multiple creative variants running (ads 999324276013320, 925342160542612). (3) Live-news messaging at $45.99/mo. A 1-Day Pass product at $4.99 is also being tested. Sling's top-ranked creative (2141016083415788) features influencer Annie Agar ("if the streaming services had a meeting"), running 26 days.

**Fubo** — Baseline posture: almost entirely FIFA World Cup 2026. English-language and Spanish-language (Fubo Latino/Telemundo) variants are running simultaneously, each per-team (Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, USA, Colombia, France, Spain, etc.). A Cash App co-promotion offers $10/mo off the first two months (ad 843493118480469). One non-World-Cup thread: "Vale Todo" telenovela premiere on Fubo Latino (ads 3277381575793429, 2761737557529790), running 26 days and ranked in top 5.

**Hulu + Live TV** — Baseline posture: three layers. (1) Disney+/Hulu duo bundle acquisition at $12.99/mo — the dominant volume, anchored on current content (The Testaments, Malcolm in the Middle, Zootopia 2, Deli Boys S2, Daredevil). (2) Hulu + Live TV acquisition, including FIFA World Cup placement and NHL Stanley Cup Playoffs creative. (3) Organic content-engagement posts (Grey's Anatomy, The Kardashians, Love Island UK, The Testaments) with no acquisition CTA — a brand-awareness layer no competitor is running at scale. Top-performing ads (2060651601426736, 741996424928454) offering "95+ channels including Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN" have run 193 days.

**YouTube TV** — No Meta ads observed in this snapshot. Website presence confirmed (first observation 2026-06-15).

---

## Patterns Across the Set

**Live sports is the organizing event for the upper tier of the market.** Sling, Fubo, and Hulu + Live TV have all pivoted significant paid creative toward the FIFA World Cup 2026 (Jun 11–Jul 19). Fubo has essentially replaced its evergreen library with match-specific creative. Sling is using the World Cup as a hook to introduce its $19.99 Essentials tier (ESPN). Hulu is threading it into its Live TV acquisition funnel. This creates a clear audience partition: sports-first viewers are being intensely contested by three services simultaneously, while comfort-TV and reality viewers are comparatively underserved in paid social right now. Philo sits entirely outside the sports conversation — by choice and by catalog — and that is currently a non-issue, but the post-World Cup period (late July onward) will see all three services pivot back to entertainment messaging, increasing pressure on Philo's lane.

**Free trial and price anchoring are now table stakes below Philo's price point.** Frndly's $6.99/7-day free trial cadence, Sling's $19.99 Essentials entry point, and Hulu's $12.99/mo bundle pricing all give consumers explicit numbers to shop. Philo's copy uses soft value language ("big entertainment, even bigger savings"; "tons of great TV") without grounding the price claim, except in a single ad. The one notable exception — ad 1487361086172161 citing $25/mo with a "5-star review" frame — is not a top-ranked creative. Hulu's longest-running top ads (192–193 days) prominently feature "95+ channels" as a channel-count frame, which Philo also doesn't use.

---

## Whitespace / Opportunities

- **Explicit price comparison vs. cable**: No competitor in the set is running a direct cable-bill comparison ad ("You're paying $X/mo for cable — Philo is $25/mo"). Sling alludes to it ("save up to $37/mo vs. YouTube TV," ad 1386598519978183) but that's intra-SVOD, not cable. Hypothesis: a "Your cable bill vs. Philo" creative using a mock invoice format could generate strong engagement with cord-cutters in consideration mode.

- **Comfort-TV genre targeting while sports rivals are occupied**: During the World Cup window (through Jul 19), Sling, Fubo, and Hulu are directing spend toward sports audiences. Philo owns shows that index heavily with women 35–65 (reality, true crime, BET, Hallmark-adjacent). Hypothesis: a burst of genre-specific comfort-TV creative during this window would face lower competitive CPMs in those audience segments.

- **Winback with a specific offer**: Philo's retargeting (`winback-facebook-retargeting`) uses generic "there's never been a better time to come back" copy (ads 2190489371707138, 856585953554761). No concrete re-join offer (e.g., first month free, $X off) is visible. Frndly's 7-day free trial is visible in every ad. Hypothesis: a winback ad with a time-limited offer ("come back this month, first month $15") would outperform the current generic tone.

- **Creator-as-discovery for niche genre audiences**: Philo's existing influencer wave (Eden Yonas, 365binge, Big Teezus) appears to target Black audiences for BET/ALLBLK content — a legitimate and differentiated angle. No competitor is doing this. Hypothesis: extending the creator format to true-crime, reality TV, and Hallmark-adjacent micro-influencers could unlock cost-efficient audience segments where Hulu and Sling aren't spending.

- **No competitor is running a "cancel anytime / no contract" message** except a single Frndly ad that mentions it in body text. Flexibility messaging (distinct from price) is absent across the set. Hypothesis: a "no contracts, cancel anytime, still cheaper than cable" ad unit would stand out in a category where every competitor's copy focuses on what you get, not the terms under which you can leave.

## Recommended Actions (Next 7 Days)

1. **Launch a price-anchor ad with a direct cable-bill comparison** [med] — Create one new Meta video/static using a visual comparison of a typical cable bill ($100+/mo) vs. Philo Essential ($25/mo). Test against the existing "tons of great TV" acquisition copy to measure CVR lift. This is the single biggest gap vs. the competitive set.

2. **Shift budget toward comfort-TV genre audiences while sports rivals are distracted** [low effort] — Existing show-specific creative (Bridezillas, Tyler Perry titles, true crime) is already built. Reallocate 15–20% of ASC spend toward female 35–65 interest segments for the World Cup window duration (through ~Jul 19). No new creative needed.

3. **Build a winback ad with a concrete re-join incentive** [med] — Replace generic "there's never been a better time to come back" with a specific offer visible in the creative itself (e.g., first month at $15, or 30 free days). Test on Facebook against the existing winback static (ad 856585953554761). Frndly's persistent 7-day free-trial framing is the competitive baseline to beat.

4. **Expand the creator program to true-crime and reality-TV influencers on Meta** [med] — The existing BET/ALLBLK creator wave is differentiated and unmatched by rivals. Replicate the format for 2–3 creators indexing with true-crime or Bravo-adjacent audiences to open a new acquisition channel before Hulu/Sling return from sports mode.

5. **Monitor Sling's $19.99 Essentials tier positioning** [low effort] — Sling is actively testing whether a stripped-down $19.99 package changes its competitive positioning against Philo's $25 entry point. Track which Essentials creative gets top-ranked over the next 7–14 days; if it scales, Philo will need a direct response framing why $25 + content depth beats $19.99 + ESPN-only.
